A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Med-Scout. Their main text and Appendices A–E are readable, including figures, tables, algorithms and equations. Relocated and reformatted material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original pilot experiments, model post-training, medical VQA and report-generation evaluations, ablations, and attention and energy analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds prompting controls, larger-model comparisons, reward ablations and qualitative case studies.

M1.justification: The standard Med-Scout tasks, GRPO procedure and reward equations remain unchanged. Appendix C.5 introduces an experimental MRL variant that adds a logical-validity reward to reasoning-mode training. This is a limited objective adaptation, not a replacement of the main method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CT, MRI and X-ray training sources, Med-Scout-Bench, six external VQA benchmarks and two report-generation benchmarks. New experiments vary prompts, rewards or models within retained coverage. Appendix E's additional modalities and longitudinal tasks remain future proposals.

E2.justification: v2 Table 6 substantially expands Med-Scout-Bench comparisons to larger models: Qwen2.5-VL-32B/72B, Qwen3-VL-32B, MedGemma-27B-IT, HuatuoGPT-Vision-34B and Lingshu-32B. Existing comparators remain. Jigsaw-R1 and ViCrit were already evaluated in v1; their appearance in the main text is not a new comparator addition.

E3.justification: v2 adds CoT conditions to the existing 200-sample pilot experiments, logical-reward training conditions, and additional backbone configurations for proxy-task and reward comparisons. The retained experiments keep their training split, 7,200-step budget, hyperparameters and primary evaluation procedures. Figure 1's expanded pilot settings are newly disclosed details.

E4.justification: v2 adds controls testing whether CoT prompting alleviates pilot failures and whether rewarding reasoning validity improves performance. It also adds two lesion-localization case studies and extends sparse-versus-dense reward analysis to Qwen3-VL-4B. These substantially broaden scrutiny of the proposed mechanism. The four-model energy analysis already existed in v1's appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests for the benchmark comparisons. The retained distribution plots are unchanged. Repeating pilot experiments with CoT introduces a different condition, not an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for CoT controls, six larger baselines, logical rewards, additional backbone comparisons and localization cases while retaining the main VQA/report-generation scores. The 4B proxy comparison also changes numerically: v1 Table 9's Med-Scout scores imply radiological/general averages of 61.4/40.5, whereas v2 Table 4 reports 60.8/40.2. Both describe sparse rewards; the PDFs do not establish why these reported values changed.

T1.justification: The reward equations, data-generation algorithms and Appendix D's manifold definition and energy-separation argument are retained. Removing repeated numerical energy gaps from prose and relocating their figure do not change the mathematical reasoning. No new formal proof accompanies the logical-reward experiment.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: geometric-blindness diagnosis, geometry-aware RL, Med-Scout-Bench and downstream transfer improvements. The headline improvement claims remain unchanged. Greater emphasis on clinical inspiration elaborates the rationale without changing the main contribution's scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 newly argues that pilot failures persist beyond prompting choices, and Appendix C.5 interprets mixed logical-reward results as showing limited benefits from explicit textual reasoning. Appendix E expands the clinical-reading interpretation and modality-specific future directions. The existing model-scale and modality limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 Figure 1 supplies pilot prompts and metric definitions, and the project link changes from a project website to a repository. Conversely, v1 Appendix B.2/Table 4's per-model GPU-hour estimates and 96GB memory specification disappear. The main hyperparameter table, training steps and GPU type remain documented.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works. The contrast with general-purpose proxy tasks such as Jigsaw-R1 and ViCrit was already made in v1 Appendix C.6; its expanded main-text presentation preserves that research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 revises introductory explanations, expands and renames Perspectives, promotes the proxy-task comparison into Section 5.7, and adds conflict-of-interest, acknowledgment and impact statements. Publication and affiliation text also changes. Most prose and the overall section hierarchy remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redesigned with protocol and clinical-motivation panels. v2 adds CoT and logical-reward tables and two case figures, restructures the proxy comparison into grouped averages, and compresses several tables. v1 Figure 13 becomes main-text Figure 6, while the training-cost table is removed.

improvement.justification: The added controls and larger-model comparisons modestly strengthen scrutiny of the geometric-perception explanation, while clearer pilot documentation improves inspectability. These gains are limited by an underspecified logical reward, removal of GPU-hour estimates and numerical inconsistencies in v2 Table 4—for example, 58.1 to 57.6 is labeled a 0.7-point decrease. The core findings and theoretical argument remain unchanged.
